_comment: Pinned third-party targets behind the held-out precision measurement reported in README.md. This file exists because the 2026-07-29 measurement retained no evidence -- no target SHAs, no scan artifacts -- which made a public claim unreproducible. Every target below was re-cloned, re-scanned at the recorded SHA, and every finding hand-audited to ground truth on 2026-07-30. These repo names are already disclosed in README.md; pinning them here adds no new disclosure and is required for the claim to be checkable. Do NOT delete a row when a target moves upstream -- add a new dated block, so the before/after stays meaningful.

measurement.scanner_analysis_note: git diff 2d93061 b508e1c -- mcp_scanner/ is empty: the commits between the 2026-07-29 measurement and this one touched only CI, README frontmatter, and the PyPI distribution name. Zero analysis code changed, so this run is comparable to the 07-29 figures.
measurement.method: Per target: read the detector source to enumerate the real sink list (never assumed), clone upstream at the recorded SHA, run `PYTHONPATH=. python -m mcp_scanner.cli <clone>`, then ground-truth EVERY finding by reading the flagged code and its callers independently of the scanner. A finding counts REAL only if attacker-controlled input can actually reach the sink in a way that matters.

followup_2026_07_30_recall_fixes._comment: The `measurement` block above is the baseline AT SCANNER b508e1c and is a historical record -- do NOT read it as current state. Three recall fixes landed the same day and changed the numbers.
fixes: slice 1 (42b61da): tool-registry extraction for the five real registration idioms
slice 2 (5654cb3): un-gate auth_posture's text-shaped checks from the Python AST
slice 3 (d3c9a9d): un-gate secret_handling's name-based branch from the Python AST
followup_2026_07_30_recall_fixes.tool_registrations_found: now true on all five targets (was false on all five)
true_positives_found: airtable-mcp-server src/main.ts:54 -- network-exposure, P1/medium: app.listen(port, callback) with no host argument binds all interfaces, serving POST /mcp with no auth, no Origin validation and no DNS-rebinding protection. Detected by argument SHAPE; no '0.0.0.0' string exists in the file.
airtable-mcp-server src/e2e.test.ts:23 -- hardcoded-secret, P1/low, graded cli-only: a committed live-format Airtable PAT. Correctly excluded from the default --fail-on gate by the test-path grade.
followup_2026_07_30_recall_fixes.gate_note: --fail-on P1 against airtable now counts exactly one finding: src/main.ts:54. Caveat recorded on re-verification: the CLI short-circuits on the first qualifying finding and never prints a gate count, so 'exactly one' is derived from the JSON output, not reported by the tool. Of airtable's 17 P0/P1 findings, 16 are graded cli-only (6 shell-injection, 1 hardcoded-secret in e2e.test.ts, 9 hardcoded-secret in enhanceAirtableError.test.ts) and are excluded from the default gate.

independent_reverification_2026_07_30._comment: The 88/2 totals above were re-derived from scratch by a second pass at scanner HEAD a5768d5, BEFORE they were published to README.md. Recorded here because the first measurement retained no per-target split, which made the total unfalsifiable -- the same defect this whole lock file exists to fix.
independent_reverification_2026_07_30.comparability: git diff d3c9a9d a5768d5 -- mcp_scanner/ is EMPTY, so the re-run is directly comparable to the d3c9a9d measurement. scan_meta.scanner_version reads a5768d5 in every output.
independent_reverification_2026_07_30.per_target_note: This split is NEW data. The targets[] rows below carry the OLD b508e1c figures (2/7/0/33/11 = 53), and the followup block recorded only the bare total 88 with no split -- so an exact re-match of 88 from an independently-derived distribution is corroboration, not an echo. Every target SHA was re-verified against its pin before scanning; clones were made outside the repo tree so the lock file was never a scan input. Two passes returned byte-identical counts.

true_positive_grading.src/main.ts:54: CONFIRMED REAL. Second arg is a callback, not a host, so Node binds all interfaces; app.post('/mcp') is a mutating route; the only app.use is express.json (no auth middleware anywhere in non-test src/); transport is constructed with only sessionIdGenerator+enableJsonResponse, so no enableDnsRebindingProtection/allowedHosts/allowedOrigins. Zero 0.0.0.0 literals in the file, confirming shape-based detection. MITIGATION THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THE CLAIM: opt-in via MCP_TRANSPORT=http (default is stdio), and upstream already discloses it at main.ts:56 and in their README -- a known accepted risk, not a hidden bug.
true_positive_grading.src/e2e.test.ts:23: QUALIFIED. Value shape verified without echoing it: field AIRTABLE_API_KEY, pat prefix, length 82, exact match for pat[A-Za-z0-9]{14}\.[a-f0-9]{64}, 31 distinct chars, no placeholder markers -- so 'live-format PAT' is accurate. BUT the two lines directly above it are an upstream comment declaring it a deliberately committed read-only token scoped to a dummy table of public test data; the scanner strips comments and cannot see it. Not a security incident. Upstream's scope claim was NOT tested -- exercising a third party's credential would be unauthorized. Do not quote '2 true positives' without this caveat; the number that describes real-world value is 1.

tool_registration_reality._comment: tool_registrations_found: true is a boolean that flips on >=1 registration. It is accurate and it over-reads badly. Extraction is exact on three targets and a near-total miss on two.

notion-mcp-server.quality: unnamed (inline); actual derived from OpenAPI operation count in scripts/notion-openapi.json, an indirect estimate

tool_registration_reality.consequence: Anything keying off the tool registry remains effectively blind on neon and notion.

not_verified: The honesty_note sub-breakdown (9 tool-scope-creep, 14 synthetic fixture credentials) was not independently audited.
Whether the airtable PAT is genuinely read-only and scoped as upstream claims.

followup_2026_07_30_recall_fixes.honesty_note: Findings rose 53 -> 88. Most of the increase is NOT true positives: 9 tool-scope-creep on airtable's mutating tools, 14 synthetic fixture credentials in test files, and assorted P3 repo-level posture findings -- all graded or demoted appropriately and kept out of the default gate. The precision layer still does not exist for JS/TS; these fixes attacked recall.

_recall_note: The 0/53 figure measures PRECISION -- of what was reported, none was real. It says nothing about recall, and the hand audit found real security-relevant issues the scanner missed entirely: an unauthenticated all-interfaces HTTP transport and a committed live-format credential in airtable-mcp-server, an unbounded local file read in firecrawl-mcp-server, and a latent unguarded path read in notion-mcp-server. In two of those cases the scanner OWNS a detector for the class (auth_posture, secret_handling's name-based branch) but gates it on a Python AST and so never runs it on .ts. Do not quote 0/53 as evidence of a clean result on these repos; it is evidence about the findings that were produced, not about the repos.
